findings.asked: Work out the numbers from each age group in a stratified sample.
findings.wentWrong: Mostly full marks; the rest were blank or wrong throughout, with the occasional slip in one age group only.
findings.rule: Group share of the sample = group size / population x sample size.

findings.asked: Estimate a population from a marked sample and a second sample, then give one fault and one improvement of the method.
findings.wentWrong: Only about a quarter got the estimate; most did not recognise the proportion argument. Some who did left a decimal number of animals. Critiques were often generic (sample size) rather than about the method described.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Set the proportion marked in the second sample equal to the proportion marked in the population, solved, and rounded to a whole number; then criticised the specific procedure in the question.
findings.rule: Marked in sample / sample size = marked in population / population; give whole animals and a fault tied to the given method.

findings.asked: Reason about whether a sample of a given size, with a given percentage, represents a population.
findings.wentWrong: Even strong candidates overthought it and listed memorised points about representativeness. Those who calculated 30% of 142 and compared it with the population got the marks.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Did the one calculation the data allowed and compared numbers, not principles.
findings.rule: When numbers are given, calculate with them; a reasoning mark comes from the specific data.

findings.asked: Stratified sample using frequencies read from a histogram.
findings.wentWrong: Only a small proportion finished; most had never got the frequencies right, and of those who had, many did not scale the group counts to the sample size.
findings.rule: Sample from a group = (group frequency / total) x sample size, rounded to a whole number.

ruleToRemember: Stratified: each group gets the same fraction of the sample as it has of the population. Population estimate: proportion marked in the second sample = proportion marked in the population. Answers are whole people; criticisms must name the fault in the given method.
aStarSignal: Doing the sampling calculation from frequencies that first had to be read off a histogram, and writing a data-specific reason rather than a memorised one.
